value.chosen_by: the feasible option needing the least propellant, then the lowest peak deceleration

capture.source: 48-catch/catch.js run(): every option evaluated; corridors by bisection on the entry angle through the 3-DOF flight

value.frame: geocentric ICRF/J2000 axes; TDB; latitude geocentric; longitude through ERFA's Earth rotation angle (UT1 = UTC), precession and nutation ignored

entry_interface.source: 48-catch/catch.js hyperbolaEntry()/stateFromLocal(): the state at the entry interface of the chosen option

value.label: Apollo-derived capsule
value.source: TransHab/Ellipsled aerocapture study (NTRS 20000102372): 6500 kg, 4.42 m, 15.34 m^2, C_L 0.466, C_D 1.269 (constant, as the study flew it)
assumed: stagnation-point radius = half the diameter, the convention of the Apollo heating analysis (NASA TN D-6843: "radius, 6.417 feet (one-half the maximum diameter)"), before its spherical-segment adjustment, which is not on file

value.atmosphere: US 1976 (PartForge isa) to 86 km, none above

retarget.source: 48-catch/catch.js (B-plane distance over the time to go)

refusals.reason: Sunlight is not modelled: no spacecraft area per mass is given (the chain has no spacecraft yet). It is not small: JPL's OSIRIS-APEX predict, flown here without it, drifts 9,400 km from JPL's in 200 days of 2026 (it fits 0.013 m^2/kg, oracle), and a TCM can absorb it only if it is modelled.
refusals.what_would_help: The spacecraft's sunlit area, mass and reflectivity (set the area per mass here).

refusals.reason: The asteroid's own orbit uncertainty is not mapped to the arrival: the spacecraft is delivered relative to where Aster's elements put it, and the approach (optical navigation) that cuts the target's uncertainty is module 42's.
refusals.what_would_help: The orbit's covariance from JPL's Small-Body Database, and approach optical navigation (module 42).

refusals.reason: 27 Delta-DOR baseline sessions found no hour with both stations above 10 deg: the spacecraft's declination puts it out of their common sky.
refusals.what_would_help: Another agency's antennas for a north-south baseline (ESA, as Lucy's paper notes), or fewer sessions.

refusals.reason: The chain has no spacecraft yet: this radio is Dawn (asteroids Vesta and Ceres)'s (DESCANSO article 13), not this mission's.
refusals.what_would_help: The mission's own transponder, amplifier, antenna and coding (a telecom design control table).

refusals.reason: The command uplink is not computed: the sources give no HGA receive gain and receiver noise for these presets, so command rates and uplink margins are not stated.
refusals.what_would_help: The spacecraft receiver's noise temperature and the HGA receive gain (an uplink DCT).

refusals.reason: 61 day(s) (2026-07-03 to 2029-04-21) put more than -85 dBm into the 34-m receiver, the recommended maximum (810-005 104 Table 7): the high-gain antenna is too loud so close to the Earth.
refusals.what_would_help: A low-gain antenna or the station's low-gain mode (-65 dBm) for those days.

refusals.reason: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s mass has not been measured: GM 2.68 m^3/s^2 is the OSIRIS-APEX team's estimate (1.36 to 4.37). Orbits and hover costs near it move with it.
refusals.what_would_help: A radio-science mass from a spacecraft at the body (as OSIRIS-REx measured Bennu's; OSIRIS-APEX will measure Apophis's).

refusals.reason: NEAR Shoemaker as built carried 318 kg of propellant (1450 m/s); this approach needs 4273 m/s, so the tanks are sized to 1654 kg with the dry mass held at 487 kg, which understates a real redesign (bigger tanks weigh more).
refusals.what_would_help: A spacecraft designed for this arrival, or a transfer with a smaller arrival v-infinity (idea 39).

refusals.reason: Gravity is a point mass: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4)'s shape and spin are not in it, so orbits within a few radii are not right here.
refusals.what_would_help: A shape model and density (module 43, Lumpy).

refusals.reason: The chain has no spacecraft yet: the engine is NEAR Shoemaker's (NSSDCA: 450 N, 1450 m/s from 318 kg on 487 kg dry, so 294.2 s effective), the sunlit area per mass OSIRIS-APEX's (AAS 24-063: 81.119 kg/m^2).
refusals.what_would_help: The mission's own spacecraft: dry mass, tanks, engines and their specific impulse, sunlit area.

refusals.reason: Uniform density: the field is the shape filled evenly. At Bennu the measured field (Scheeres et al. 2020, Table 1) has J2 2.7% and J3 15.8% larger than its constant-density shape gives, surface gravity differs by up to ±3% and slopes by ±1°, and the constant-density stable equilibrium is unstable in the measured field.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured gravity field: radio tracking from orbit (OSIRIS-REx at Bennu; OSIRIS-APEX at Apophis from 2029).

refusals.reason: Apophis's tumbling needs inertia ratios 0.61 and 0.965 (Pravec et al. 2014); the radar shape filled evenly gives 0.730 and 0.947. Uniform density cannot be the whole truth (or the shape is off), so the field beyond GM carries that doubt.
refusals.what_would_help: A shape from OSIRIS-APEX imaging and a measured field.

refusals.reason: 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) tumbles (Pravec et al. 2014): no frame turns with it at a constant rate, so its field never stands still in one and it has no equilibrium points or rotational Roche lobe.
refusals.what_would_help: Nothing: they do not exist for a tumbler. Hovering costs Delta-v everywhere (idea 42's station-keeping).

refusals.reason: The shape's plates are 25 m across: slopes and gravity under a lander's footprint (metres) are not resolved, and slopes here are smoother than at that scale (Bennu's 3 m model averages 17°).
refusals.what_would_help: OSIRIS-APEX's imaging shape model (2029).

refusals.reason: The descent and back-away need 0.946 m/s, 0.160 kg of propellant at Isp 294.2 s; the chain's spacecraft reaches the stand-off with 0.103 kg (idea 42's mass block).
refusals.what_would_help: More propellant at launch (idea 42's tankage), a lighter spacecraft, or a slower departure leg.

refusals.reason: The site is a 105 m^2 plate of idea 43's 25 m shape: boulders, craters and slopes at the scale of the 8 m safe radius and the 0.32 m sampler head are not in it, so the chance of an unsafe contact is not computed (only the chance of landing inside the safe radius).
refusals.what_would_help: A local terrain model from OSIRIS-APEX imaging, then a hazard map.

refusals.reason: The regolith's resistance is Bennu's at Nightingale (inferred from NASA's 48.8 cm in ~6 s at 10 cm/s), carried to 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) as an analog: nothing has touched its surface.
refusals.what_would_help: The spacecraft's accelerometer record of the contact (Walsh et al. 2022, Sci. Adv.) or, for another body, a touch.

refusals.reason: No particle-size map of 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4) exists, and TAGSAM-class collection depends on the smallest and largest particles and their size distribution (Walsh et al. 2022); the sample mass is not computed. The Nightingale analog below is labelled as such.
refusals.what_would_help: Imaging at better than 1 cm/pixel of the site (OSIRIS-APEX), then the sampleability algorithm.

refusals.reason: Anchors that rely on the ground's strength (harpoons, screws) are not modelled: Bennu's near surface is "loosely packed and lightly bound" (NASA, 2022), and no strength is known for 99942 Apophis (2004 MN4). Holding down is by weight and thrust only.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured cohesion or an anchor pull test in situ.

refusals.reason: For an S-type the water is the 160–510 ppm Itokawa's returned grains carry in their pyroxene and olivine (Jin and Bose 2019), all of it counted: how much an oven at 750 °C releases from nominally anhydrous minerals is not measured in these sources, so every water number here is an upper bound.
refusals.what_would_help: A heating experiment on an ordinary chondrite (LL) or on Itokawa grains, with the water measured against temperature and time.

refusals.reason: Digging resistance is idea 44's fit to OSIRIS-REx's 10 cm/s contact at Bennu (69–165 Pa), used as the pressure on a drum's cut face; nothing has been excavated in milligravity, and the drums' own forces were measured only in lunar simulant at 1 g (IPEx), where the vertical force was the weight of the regolith caught: whether a cut lifts a lander that weighs millinewtons is not measured, and not modelled here.
refusals.what_would_help: An excavation test in the target's regolith, or in a simulant on a reduced-gravity flight, with the vertical force measured.

refusals.reason: The horizon is the site plate's own plane: shadows from boulders and the rest of the body are not cast (idea 43's shapes have 25 m plates). Set a horizon mask to be conservative.
refusals.what_would_help: A terrain model at metre scale and a ray-traced horizon.

refusals.reason: Digging 10.0 mm deep pushes the spacecraft 33.6 mN sideways (the drums' cutting imbalance and the dug regolith brought to its speed); with the slope's own 5.7 mN along the ground the feet need a friction coefficient of 0.86 against 45.8 mN of weight on the ground (0.13 for the slope alone). No friction is measured for this regolith, so whether the feet slip is not judged.
refusals.what_would_help: A friction coefficient for the feet on this regolith (set one here as a what-if), or propellant to cancel the sideways push with thrust.

refusals.reason: Idea 45's water is an upper bound (all of Itokawa's 510 ppm counted as released), so every propellant figure here is an upper bound too.
refusals.what_would_help: A measured water release for this asteroid's rock (idea 45's "release" refusal).

refusals.reason: The electrolyser's mass, and its pumps, dryers and power conditioning, are not on file (DOE gives $/kW and kWh/kg, not kg/kW); it is assumed to stay on the asteroid and is not in the return dry mass.
refusals.what_would_help: A flight electrolyser's mass per kW (the ISS OGA's, for instance).

refusals.reason: Array power is scaled as 1/r² from its 1 au value, ignoring cell temperature: checked only beyond 1 au, where it reads 7.0 % low for NEAR at 2.2 au and 3.5 to 17 % low for Psyche; this stay is inside 1 au, where hotter cells make it likely optimistic.
refusals.what_would_help: The array's measured power against Sun distance and temperature.

refusals.reason: Delivered Isp is the shifting ideal times 0.9791, the RL10A-3-3's published/ideal at O/F 5 (SP-8120 Table I). At O/F 7.94 that factor is carried, not measured; no flown hydrogen-oxygen engine on file runs there.
refusals.what_would_help: Hot-fire data for a hydrogen-oxygen engine at this mixture ratio.

refusals.reason: Cryogenic tank walls, insulation blankets and supports are not given a mass (they are set by minimum gauge and structure, not by pressure, and none are on file); their volumes and areas are computed.
refusals.what_would_help: A small flight cryogenic tank's mass per litre.

refusals.reason: The heat leak is MHTB's 45-layer insulation on an 18 m³ tank, 0.22 W/m² at 305 K; tanks this small (11.3 L of hydrogen) leak more per m² through supports and pipes, so boil-off here is a lower bound.
refusals.what_would_help: Heat-leak data for a tank of this size.

refusals.reason: No 90 K cryocooler's measured efficiency or mass is on file: the 90 K stage is costed at 13.95 % of Carnot (the 20 K unit's at full lift, NASA/Creare 2026), 16.73 W per W, and given no mass.
refusals.what_would_help: A flight 90 K cryocooler's measured input power and mass (NASA's 150 W class).

refusals.reason: There are no batteries: coolers and electrolyser run only while the Sun is up at the site, and the tanks boil in the dark.
refusals.what_would_help: A battery and its mass.

refusals.reason: The asteroid's orbit is Aster's elements (epoch 2026-05-01 TDB) integrated through idea 40's forces, without Yarkovsky or asteroid perturbers and without its orbit uncertainty. JPL's NHATS return legs, computed with JPL's own ephemerides, are the check (this page's reality table): the gap grows after an Earth encounter.
refusals.what_would_help: JPL's SPK for the body and its covariance (Horizons, or the Small-Body Database).

refusals.reason: The asteroid's own gravity is left out of the departure burn and the craft leaves from its centre of mass.
refusals.what_would_help: The escape speed from the stand-off (idea 43's field) added to the burn.

refusals.reason: The return's navigation is not analysed: the departure burn carries Aster's 10 % margin and one correction the size of its own 3-sigma execution error (Lucy's 30 mm/s + 4 %, idea 40); orbit-determination errors and the TCMs that cut them are not budgeted. The correction's propellant is counted as burned with the departure burn; kept for a correction made later, its hydrogen (0.0286 kg) would boil away in 2.8 days at the passive rate, so a later correction needs the coolers held or a separate storable thruster.
refusals.what_would_help: A covariance analysis of the return like idea 40's for the outbound (its 116.6 m/s was mostly the launcher's injection error, which does not apply here).

refusals.reason: No structure, container or heat shield is counted for the material: the craft's dry mass is idea 46's, and whatever holds the material home (and protects it at entry, module 49) is not on file.
refusals.what_would_help: A container and capsule mass (OSIRIS-REx's and Hayabusa2's capsules are the flown references).

refusals.reason: Arriving at 12.53 km/s at 125 km, above NHATS's 12 km/s entry limit: as handed on, it needs braking, aerocapture or a catch.
refusals.what_would_help: Module 48 (Catch) compares the options; or brake here to the limit (NHATS's rule).

refusals.reason: Idea 47 aims at a 123.7 km perigee, a flyby: entering at -6.502° needs a perigee at 56.44 km (B 87.71 km nearer). A correction 14 days out costs about 79.8 mm/s, 184 g of propellant; 0 kg arrives.
refusals.what_would_help: Set module 47's aim perigee to 56.44 km, so the departure burn aims at the entry (no correction at the Earth).

refusals.reason: No heat shield, structure or container mass is counted: the entry mass is the arrival mass (9565.4 kg) inside the chosen shape.
refusals.what_would_help: Module 49 (Hot Return) sizes the heat shield from this heating; a container mass for the material.

refusals.reason: Heating is Sutton & Graves's convective stagnation-point rate only ("Radiative heating was neglected", NASA TR R-376). At lunar-return speeds radiation is not small: "radiative heating is approximately one-third of the total heating rate" for Apollo (NASA TN D-6843).
refusals.what_would_help: A radiative correlation or a shock-layer solution (module 49).

refusals.reason: The atmosphere is the 1976 standard to 86 km and none above; no winds, no day-of density. OSIRIS-REx's team saw "atmospheric density being much lower than was Earth-GRAM was predicting" (OSIRIS-REx EDL performance, 2025).
refusals.what_would_help: A day-of atmosphere (GEOS forecast, GRAM dispersions) for the entry date.

refusals.reason: The vehicle's numbers are partly assumed: stagnation-point radius = half the diameter, the convention of the Apollo heating analysis (NASA TN D-6843: "radius, 6.417 feet (one-half the maximum diameter)"), before its spherical-segment adjustment, which is not on file.
refusals.what_would_help: The vehicle's own aerodynamic database and heat-shield geometry.

refusals.reason: Constant bank, no guidance: the corridors are the lift-up and lift-down bounds a guided vehicle flies between, wider than what a guidance law and its dispersions leave (the TransHab study flew bank reversals to hold its target).
refusals.what_would_help: An entry guidance law with dispersions (Monte Carlo over density, aerodynamics and the entry state).

assumptions: Time TDB inside (UTC = TDB - 69.184 s); geocentric ICRF/J2000 axes; the atmosphere rotates about the ICRF z axis at the pck00010 rate.
Earth: a sphere of 6,378,136.6 m with Aster's GM 398,600.4418 km^3/s^2; point-mass gravity (no J2) during the minutes of a pass.
Atmosphere: the 1976 US Standard (PartForge isa) to its table top at 86 km, no density above, no winds.
Vehicle: a point mass with the chosen shape's C_D (or C_A against Mach) and C_L at constant bank; deceleration = |aerodynamic acceleration| / 9.80665.

Heating: Sutton & Graves (NASA TR R-376) air coefficient K = 0.1113 with Newtonian stagnation pressure rho V^2 and stagnation enthalpy V^2/2 (cold wall): q = 1.748e-4 sqrt(rho/Rn) V^3, convective only.
The arrival hyperbola keeps idea 47's v-infinity vector and plane and is re-aimed only in its perigee (B magnitude); the perigee time is idea 47's.
Propellant: Tsiolkovsky with the arrival's exhaust speed and Aster's 10 % delta-v margin.
